pictures.author: Dirrival
pictures.observations: Whole500x667 front: specific red two-storey bell tower, real round ground passage, pale stone foot, smaller lower green eave and larger swept green hipped upper roof. Upper red shutters/arched lattice opening, blue/green/gold painted beams and small original ridge silhouettes.

pictures.author: Dirrival
pictures.observations: Whole960x720 roofed three-arch red gate, pale stone base, green swept tiled roof and painted blue/green/gold beam registers. Central passage open; paired studded red-brown leaves close side arches. File English North Holy Gate caption conflicts with Chinese South Heavenly Gate wording; correlate approximate appearance with mapped northern park entrance, not a definitive historical gate-name claim. Modern lattice mast visible behind.

pictures.author: Dirrival
pictures.observations: Whole960x720 hall: green swept hipped/gabled roof, red six-panel lattice doors, original blue/green/gold painted beam vocabulary and narrow pale stair. Named dressing-hall identity is not present on the mapped west hall; appearance allocation is approximate. No inscription, story motif or source pixels copied.

pictures.author: Dirrival
pictures.observations: Whole960x720: three roofless pale stone portals, center taller, six square posts with rounded/peach-like finials, lintel registers and original cloud-like ends. Openings are visibly blocked by gray panels/masonry, not walk-through portals. Low gray capped enclosure behind; large modern lattice transmission structure remains surrounding host context.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Standing Temple of the Moon heritage compound: mapped red double-eaved green-roofed bell tower with real ground arch and recessed upper lattice, mapped triple-arched roofed park gate with open center/closed side leaves, and mapped west hall with swept green roof/red lattice doors. Include approximate surviving gray inner enclosure/three blocked pale Lingxing portals and short mapped northern outer-wall runs. Original simplified painted-beam/ridge/finial vocabulary, no copied text/photo atlas. Do not reconstruct the no-longer-intact altar. Modern lattice transmission mast and southern park landscaping/pavilions remain host context, not part of this heritage-building model.
currentRoundInspection.identityNote: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_of_the_Moon_(China) states the altar is no longer intact. Standing structures are modeled; no hypothetical intact altar is restored.
